title: A Sentence on a Comb — Tel Lachish Canaanite Ivory Lice Comb Inscription, Microscopic Head-Louse Remains, Early Alphabetic Paleography & Barley Radiocarbon Context

teenKit.tldr: An ancient ivory comb from Tel Lachish bears the world's oldest full alphabetic sentence—a desperate anti-lice curse—complete with the actual preserved membrane of a prehistoric head louse trapped between its teeth.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that everyday people were using the newly invented alphabet for mundane hygiene complaints over 3,700 years ago, bridging the gap between grand history and our most annoying human inconveniences.
keyTakeaways: The 17 shallow Canaanite letters carved into the comb translate to a practical and dramatic plea: 'May this tusk root out the lice of the hair and the beard.'
Scientists found actual physical evidence tucked inside the comb: the outer membrane of a head-louse nymph, locking biological proof together with written history.
Researchers dated the archaeological layer precisely using AMS radiocarbon dating on short-lived barley seeds found right alongside the artifact.

quiz.question: What is unique about the inscription found on the Tel Lachish ivory comb?
options: It is the oldest known royal decree carved in gold.
It is the oldest full sentence written in the early Canaanite alphabet.
It is a magical spell designed to cure the plague.
It is a shopping list for barley and wine.
quiz.explanation: The 17 carved letters form the earliest known complete sentence using the revolutionary alphabetic writing system.

quiz.question: What microscopic biological remain was trapped between the teeth of the comb?
options: The membrane of a head-louse nymph
quiz.explanation: Researchers found the preserved membrane of a baby head louse (nymph), giving direct physical proof of what the comb was fighting.

quiz.question: How did scientists accurately determine the age of the layer where the comb was found?
options: By analyzing the style of royal pottery nearby
By translating the king's birth year mentioned in the text
By running AMS radiocarbon dating on preserved barley seeds
By measuring the thickness of the ivory tusk
quiz.explanation: Short-lived organic materials like stratified barley seeds provide reliable targets for precise radiocarbon dating.
